newsitem.title: USA: Columbia/HCA acquiring Value Health for $1.3 billion.
newsitem.headline: Columbia/HCA acquiring Value Health for $1.3 billion.

text.p: Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp., the nation's largest for-profit provider of health care services, has agreed to acquire Value Health Inc. in a $1.4 billion tax-free stock transaction.
Columbia/HCA said late Wednesday that it would issue about 35 million shares of common stock to acquire Value Health, a $1.9 billion speciality healthcare services company based in Avon, Conn.
Each Value Health stockholder will receive .58 share of Columbia common stock in exchange for each Value Health share held, the company said.
Based on Columbia/HCA's stock price Thursday morning, the deal would be worth about $1.39 billion.

Value Health has four main businesses -- the nation's largest independent pharmacy benefit management company; the largest provider of managed behavioural healthcare; a workers' compensation and group health network and cost management company; and a technology information company that develops disease management programmes.
The companies anticipate that the proposed merger, which will be accounted for as a pooling-of-interests, will close by summer.
Columbia/HCA's stock lost 62.5 cents to $39.625 in early trading Thursday on the New York Stock Exchange while Value Health jumped $2 to $22.25, also on the NYSE.
